documents.title: Standards and Recommendations for the Use of Generative AI in Teaching and Learning at Northeastern
documents.stance_why: The document says "The university supports faculty autonomy in determining appropriate AI use in their courses" and offers sample syllabus statements and assignment labels without setting one default, so the decision is handed to instructors; the tiers are listed.
documents.summary: The July 2025 provost standards support faculty autonomy: instructors decide whether AI is prohibited, permitted, encouraged or required and must state this in the syllabus and assignments. It recommends aligning AI with learning goals, disclosure, redesigned assessment, no reliance on detectors, and committee review for AI grading and data-sensitive uses.

documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy
documents.stance_why: The only AI wording is "Unauthorized use of aids such as ... artificial intelligence, chatbots"; whether a use is authorized is left to each course ("they are responsible for knowing the requirements and restrictions"), so the document sets no AI stance of its own.
documents.summary: The student conduct office's integrity policy defines cheating, fabrication, plagiarism and unauthorized collaboration; AI appears only as one example of an unauthorized aid. It describes reporting, sanctions from warning to expulsion, appeals, and instructor grade penalties.

units.why: Students "are responsible for knowing the requirements and restrictions" in each course, including "the use of study aids" and "the appropriateness of assistance"; students must learn each course's rules (P78). AI is not named in this sentence.

units.frag_start: In each course, they are responsible for knowing the requirements
units.frag_end: the appropriateness of assistance, and other issues
units.fit_note: Does not name AI; refers to study aids and assistance generally.
